title: Given K sorted integer lists, find the smallest range that includes at least one number from each of the K lists. If several ranges are equally small, return the one with the smaller start. Explain the K-way Merge technique and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Smallest Number Range Covering K Lists (Find the Tightest Range Including One Element from Each List)
keyPoints: The min-heap holds one current element per list, and a separate variable tracks the running maximum.
The window from heap-min to running-max always covers all K lists at every moment.
Advancing the minimum element is the only lever that can shrink the window.
When any list is exhausted, no further valid window can cover all lists, so the algorithm stops.
Time complexity is O(N log K) where N is the total elements across all lists.
Ties on window width are resolved by keeping the first (smaller-start) window.

s1_definition.oneliner: The window from heap-min to running-max always covers all lists; shrink it by advancing the minimum.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Smallest Number Range** is a K-way Merge problem that finds the tightest range covering all K sorted lists.
- A **min-heap** holds one current element per list, and a separate variable tracks the **running maximum**.
- The span from heap minimum to running maximum is always a valid covering range.
- We repeatedly **advance the minimum** to try to shrink the window, updating the best range.
- When any list is **exhausted**, no further valid window exists, so we stop.
- Time is **O(N log K)** and space is **O(K)**.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has K sorted lists of home-loan interest rates from K lenders. The marketing team wants the narrowest rate band that still contains at least one genuine quote from every lender. A clerk keeps the current lowest unused rate per lender on a tray, notes the highest of those rates, and the band from lowest to highest covers everyone. The clerk nudges the lowest rate forward, trying to shrink the band, and remembers the tightest band seen.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Smallest Number Range Covering K Lists is a K-way Merge problem built on one clean invariant. If the min-heap holds exactly one element from each list, then the span from the smallest to the largest of those elements must contain at least one number from every list. You keep the heap minimum and separately track the running maximum of whatever is currently in the heap.

To shrink the range, you repeatedly record the current span, pop the minimum, and push its successor from the same list while updating the running maximum. Advancing the minimum is the only lever that can tighten the window because the maximum can only stay or rise. The instant any list runs out, no further window can cover all lists, so you stop. Ties on width are resolved toward the smaller start.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this to advertise the tightest home-loan rate band that still included at least one genuine quote from every lender. The marketing team needed honest advertising that represented all lenders fairly. Rajesh kept one live rate per lender in the heap, tracked the running maximum, and remembered the narrowest covering band across all iterations.

The senior-level insight is understanding why both the invariant and the stopping condition are correct: the heap-min-to-running-max span always covers all lists because each list has exactly one representative, and exhaustion terminates because coverage can no longer be maintained. Explaining these two points clearly is what distinguishes a strong answer.

Remember one sentence: the window from heap-min to running-max covers all K lists; shrink it by advancing the minimum until a list runs out.
